findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Employee reporting agreements or another similar verification is not available during this inspection. A copy of the reporting agreement given out by SCDPH was given to the facility. They made multiple copies and had staff sign during the inspection to correct.

findings.comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.comment: 750-100 Facility is operating as a High Risk based on the menu (population and permit are Medium Risk),. Children's Recreation Club would like to remain a Medium Risk facility. The cooling of casseroles will cease. Foods will be cooked and served for a single event only. All leftovers will be discarded or taken home. The remaining pizza casserole is going home with staff. Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: 750-151(a) Two packages of sliced deli meats are observed opened and without a label. Packages were dated with 2/27 during the inspection. The Seven Day Rule was discussed with staff.  Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment: 750-160 There is observed stained mildew on a linen being used for a cold compress, but being held in the freezer. Thye compress was discarded during the inspection. Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-160 The second refrigerator is observed with a serious accumulation of molds and moisture in the basin of the unit. Unit is being cleaned and bleached. See that equipment is regularly cleaned and servicxed to avoid the accumulation of molds and condensation. Also, see violation #41. There are air fresheners and chemical bottles observed on baking sheets and cutting boards within the kitchen. Watch that this practice is stopped in order to prevent chemicals from contaminating food handling equipment.   Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment: 750-530a. Observed employee beverages stored (frozen to the interior ceiling) on the top shelf of the second refrigerator. Keep personal foods stored on the lowest possible shelf of the refrigerator or in a tub large enough to hold all products.  Employees shall consume food only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-600 The freezer of the second refrigerator is observed with frost accumulation. Also, the personal beverages being stored in the second cooler are locked to the fridge by a brick of ice. Defrost these two surfaces. Finally, there is a piece of laminate edging pulling away from the countertop on the left side. Seal the laminate to the counter. Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b There are at least four wet cloths observed draped over the dividers of the triple sink. Cloths are from yesterday's use. See that all soiled linens are removed from service and properly washed or stored in a soiled linen container separate from clean dish storage areas.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the triple sink basins to be soiled with old paint. Clean the sinks after each use.  To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e Observed the inside of the far right cabinet underneath the prepartion counter (saw dust) and the refrigerators (food spill) to be soiled. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: 750-1120e The handsink is observed without soap and paper toweling. Both were provided during the inspection. Keep handsoap and towels available for quick and proper handwashing. A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment: 750-1170 A wasp was observed resting on silverware in the kitchen. Killed during the inspection. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1160 Observed the window adjacent to the triple sink to have an improper seal around a window air conditioning unit. The window unit has gaps around the sides that are being sealed with weather striping and plastic bags. In addition to the hole from the air conditioning unit, there is an air return with a vented cover on this same wall. The vent looks like an old vent for the hood that has been improperly capped. The cap should be screened or solid. Seal around the AC unit using a seal board (similar to that which is observed in the common play room). Also, properly seal the vent if it is no longer necessary. Screen the vent should the it still be of purpose. Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1220 The floor behind the second refrigerator and under the triple sink is observed soiled with old food debris and possible old mouse droppings. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.
750-1200 The coving underneath the triple sink is observed pulling from the wall. Seal the coving to the wall. The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment: 750-1240 The lights in the refrigerators are not observed shielded or with a shatter proof bulb. Provide a shield or proper shatter resistant bulb.  All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage.  Provide properly shielded lights.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment: 750-1310 Observed a bottle of Air Wick, Fabreze, OdoBan, and Mr, Clean Erasers on a stack of cutting boards, plates, and baking sheets on the preparation counter. Chemicals were moved during the inspection. All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.
